oracle.scope: Canonical SQLite migration identity, ordering, history conversion, opener authority, diagnostics, backup, and restore behavior.
oracle.compatibilityRule: Only an exact canonical prefix or an exact prefix of a listed convertible legacy composition may be changed. Unknown, ambiguous, corrupt, direct-SQL, and placeholder histories remain byte-untouched and fail closed.
oracle.absenceOfDeploymentAuthority: The repository and accepted planning evidence contain no live, deployed, or externally inventoried database history. This oracle therefore freezes lossless conversion for every exact accepted ledger observed in source without inventing a data-discard policy.

baseline.databaseOpenBehavior: packages/storage/src/database.ts validates an independently supplied schema ceiling and never applies migrations
baseline.ceilingDisposition: legacy compatibility guard only; not a migration registry and not evidence that versions 1 through 11 form the application schema

checksumAuthority.foreignKeysOffMaterial: migration.sql exactly, followed by newline and /* migration-requires-foreign-keys-off:v1 */
checksumAuthority.immutability: Canonical slot, semantic id, name, SQL bytes, execution mode, and resulting checksum are append-only authority. Any semantic change requires a new final slot.
checksumAuthority.sourceVersionRule: A migration module's declared version records its legacy local composition only. The canonical registry clones the unchanged semantic definition with the canonical slot. The accepted search-reindex schema was never ledgered and therefore retains declaredVersion null plus legacyRecorded false instead of receiving an invented historical version.

canonicalRegistry.orderRule: Ascending first-accepted commit ancestry at shaping commit 547f70dd67959541324688b7b737749bc43791ab, with dependency order inside the three migrations first accepted together at 9d1f77791c2af1c024347c462899ca645823716a.

historicalPolicy.supported: The empty database, every exact canonical prefix, and every exact non-empty prefix of a convertible ledger composition below, combined only with an exact supported search-reindex schema overlay.
historicalPolicy.classification: Require user_version to equal ledger row count, versions to be contiguous from one, every recorded row name and checksum to identify exactly one frozen semantic migration, recorded semantic identities to be unique, dependencies to be present earlier or provably represented by the exact schema, the base SQLite schema fingerprint to match the expected ledger result, and the search-reindex overlay to satisfy one exact overlay state. The unledgered search-reindex semantic is never fabricated as an old ledger row.
historicalPolicy.schemaFingerprint: Decode one complete supported ledger sequence, then build its expected base schema in isolated in-memory SQLite from the exact frozen semantic definitions at the decoded contiguous positions. Compare the complete ordered tuple sequence and its digest, encoded as UTF-8 JSON.stringify of [type,name,tbl_name,sql] rows from sqlite_schema with SQLite null encoded as JSON null. Exclude only sqlite_ internals, exact fully validated schema_migrations infrastructure, exact fully validated conversion-provenance infrastructure and rows, and one fully classified reindex overlay. Never use a literal object allowlist, selected-table presence, unchecked name prefix, or digest without tuple equality; any added or changed table, index, trigger, or view is unsupported before a source effect.
historicalPolicy.schemaOverlayRule: Classify the unledgered search-reindex schema independently. Absent and exact empty one-table partial states are completed by canonical slot 20. Exact idle, both building-empty variants, nonempty building, or activating states preserve their control rows and deterministic replacement FTS objects; every active state accepts any operation name matching reindexAuthority.operationNamePattern and verifies the frozen name derivation and row/object relations. Any other control DDL, lease, progress, replacement name, object family, counter, digest, or orphan state is unsupported before write.
historicalPolicy.conversionBackup: Before changing a file-backed legacy database, automatically publish and verify one complete backup in the configured privateRoot/backups directory, outside the mutable data, blob, journal, and configuration subtrees. Conversion does not begin if backup creation or verification fails.
historicalPolicy.conversionTransaction: Disable foreign keys before BEGIN IMMEDIATE, archive the exact legacy ledger, overlay classification, and their digests in immutable registry metadata, execute each missing semantic SQL body once in canonical slot order, preserve any valid active reindex actor state, validate integrity and foreign keys, replace schema_migrations with all 27 canonical rows, set user_version to 27, commit, and restore foreign_keys=ON. Any failure before commit rolls back the entire database conversion.
historicalPolicy.conversionFeasibility: At the shaping commit, every one of the 44 convertible full ledgers and all 76 unique non-empty prefixes can execute its missing frozen SQL bodies, including absent search-reindex control schema, inside one foreign-keys-off BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction and reach the same 192 application schema objects with integrity ok and no foreign-key findings. Focused overlay probes cover absent, partial-empty, idle, both building-empty variants, nondefault nonempty building, and nondefault activating states plus forged negatives. This proves schema feasibility only; issue 234 must still prove ledger archival, backup, domain-row parity, and injected rollback.
historicalPolicy.dataRule: No table, row, blob reference, or accepted provenance may be dropped as a compatibility shortcut. Existing semantic SQL is skipped only after exact identity plus schema proof.
historicalPolicy.unknownRule: A missing ledger on a non-empty database, nonzero user_version without a ledger, unknown name or checksum, duplicate semantic identity, unexpected schema object, dependency contradiction, placeholder, direct-SQL bypass, or ambiguous fingerprint returns a stable unsupported-history error before any write.
historicalPolicy.prefixRule: An error or crash before an ordinary migration commit leaves its exact canonical predecessor; after commit it leaves the newly committed exact canonical prefix. An error or crash before the legacy conversion commit leaves the exact legacy ledger and reindex overlay; after commit it leaves exact canonical 27 with the same valid active overlay. Reopen always reclassifies ledger plus schema and never infers success from selected schema objects alone.

reindexAuthority.operationNameEncoding: UTF-8 bytes of the exact operation name; no trim, normalization, or case folding
reindexAuthority.replacementNameDerivation: message_fts_replacement_ plus the first 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters of SHA-256(operationName UTF-8 bytes)
reindexAuthority.replacementObjectTupleDerivation: For each valid operation name, create the derived replacement virtual table with the byte-frozen external-content FTS5 SQL in isolated in-memory SQLite, then freeze and compare every ordered [type,name,tbl_name,sql] tuple for the virtual table and all four SQLite-generated shadow tables. Names alone, docsize presence, selected rows, or a digest without tuple equality never establish the family.
reindexAuthority.leaseRelation: Exactly zero or one lease_id=1 row. A row's operation_name matches the grammar, replacement_name equals the frozen derivation, phase is building or activating, and last_rowid/processed_rows are safe nonnegative integers.
reindexAuthority.progressRelation: Every progress row uses the lease replacement_name, has a unique positive source_rowid and a lowercase SHA-256 source_digest, and has a matching replacement FTS rowid. No progress exists without a lease and exact replacement family.
reindexAuthority.counterRelation: Building-empty requires last_rowid=processed_rows=0 and no progress/replacement rows. Nonempty building requires processed_rows=progress count=replacement docsize count, last_rowid=max progress source_rowid, and an exact digest match to indexed_messages for every processed row. Activating additionally requires processed_rows=source/progress/replacement counts and last_rowid=max indexed_messages rowid, or zero for an empty source.
forgedCases: replacement name not derived from operation name
missing, altered, extra, or multiply named replacement object
progress digest or FTS rowid mismatch
activating state without a complete replacement
lease pointing at message_fts or message_fts_previous
building-empty lease with an ordinary-table lookalike replacement family
building-empty lease with altered virtual-table or shadow-table tuple bytes
nonempty lease with an ordinary-table lookalike replacement family
nonempty lease with altered virtual-table or shadow-table tuple bytes

runtimeAuthority.singleRegistry: Every writable application database opener imports the one frozen registry. No caller supplies a schema ceiling or migration array.
runtimeAuthority.packageBoundary: The storage registry never imports the daemon. Issue 234 moves the unchanged initial-backfill-completion definition from its accepted daemon source to packages/storage/src/migrations/initial-backfill-completion.ts, then makes the daemon consume the storage-owned definition.
runtimeAuthority.derivedConstants: CANONICAL_DATABASE_SCHEMA_VERSION is registry.length and NEXT_DATABASE_MIGRATION_VERSION is schemaVersion + 1; no independent numeric ceiling is authoritative.
runtimeAuthority.conversionBackupCapability: The application opener is constructed with validated archive-root paths and one pre-conversion backup capability. It invokes that capability only after the no-source-write scratch preflight classifies an exact legacy history, targeting configured privateRoot/backups. A missing capability, failed publication, failed verification, or locked fingerprint drift rejects legacy open before the source is opened read-write; fresh and canonical-prefix opens do not invoke it.
openOrder: lstat and read a stable whole-tree plus main/WAL/SHM source snapshot without opening source SQLite or changing permissions
materialize the main/WAL bytes into unpublishable owner-only scratch outside privateRoot
open scratch, set only query_only, foreign_keys, and trusted_schema connection-local pragmas, and read the complete fingerprint
reject newer, corrupt, unknown, ambiguous, placeholder, direct-SQL, provenance-invalid, or reindex-invalid state; remove scratch with the source tree unchanged
for an exact supported legacy history, publish and independently verify the complete pre-conversion backup
acquire the exclusive application write-admission barrier
repeat the stable source snapshot plus scratch classification and require equality with preflight and backup input
only now open source SQLite read-write without create, enforce safe permissions/pragmas, and configure WAL
BEGIN IMMEDIATE and revalidate the full logical fingerprint on the write connection
convert an exact legacy history atomically or apply an exact canonical suffix, including exact provenance infrastructure and one transaction-gated row
commit, restore foreign_keys, verify integrity, history, provenance, and reindex overlay, then admit writers
return the handle only at canonical version 27 with exact canonical history
runtimeAuthority.repeatedOpen: An exact version-27 database performs no schema, history, conversion-ledger, reindex-actor, or domain write. It revalidates names, checksums, migration infrastructure, and the reindex overlay before return.
runtimeAuthority.newerVersion: user_version greater than 27 or any unknown later ledger row fails before mutation. Downgrade and automatic repair are forbidden.
runtimeAuthority.partialFailure: The transaction commit is the only registry cutover. Preflight rejection leaves the complete source tree and sidecar presence/bytes/modes unchanged. Backup or locked-revalidation failure leaves the source database unchanged and retains any verified backup. Before commit, ordinary suffix failure leaves the previous canonical prefix and legacy conversion failure leaves the original legacy history, reindex overlay, and data. After commit, the complete new canonical prefix or complete canonical 27 is authoritative even if later opener work fails. No mixed ledger/schema/provenance state is accepted; foreign keys and the persistent always-deny insertion trigger are restored on every non-crash exit.
runtimeAuthority.metadata: schema_migration_conversions is versioned migration-runner infrastructure beside schema_migrations, not an application migration slot. Registry v1 creates and verifies the byte-frozen table/index/trigger bundle in the first registry transaction. Fresh databases contain no conversion rows; converted databases preserve and digest the exact old history, base schema, overlay snapshot, target registry, verified backup identity, canonical timestamp, conversion id, and complete record.

conversionMetadata.historyEncoding: UTF-8 JSON.stringify of rows ordered by version, each encoded as [version,name,content_hash]
conversionMetadata.overlayEncoding: UTF-8 JSON.stringify(["agent-mail/search-reindex-overlay/v1",overlay_id,lease_or_null,progress_rows,schema_objects,source_rows,replacement_docsize_rowids]), where lease_or_null is null or [lease_id,operation_name,replacement_name,phase,last_rowid,processed_rows], progress_rows are [replacement_name,source_rowid,source_digest] ordered by replacement_name/source_rowid, schema_objects are [type,name,tbl_name,sql] ordered by type/name/tbl_name/sql, source_rows are [rowid,message_id,subject,participants,body_plain,body_html,attachment_names] ordered by rowid for an active lease and empty otherwise, and replacement_docsize_rowids are positive integers ordered by rowid. This makes every source digest and progress/index identity independently decodable.
conversionMetadata.schemaEncoding: UTF-8 JSON.stringify of [type,name,tbl_name,sql] rows ordered by type,name,tbl_name,sql after excluding sqlite_ objects, migration infrastructure, and the separately encoded reindex overlay; SQLite null is JSON null
conversionMetadata.digestEncoding: Each history, overlay, and schema SHA-256 is lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of its exact UTF-8 JSON bytes
conversionMetadata.timestampDomain: completed_at is exactly Date.toISOString(): 24 ASCII bytes YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ, round-trips through new Date(value).toISOString(), and is the verified backup response createdAt captured before the conversion transaction
conversionMetadata.backupIdentityDomain: backup_id is backup: plus the published backup directory label matching [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}; backup_manifest_sha256 is the independently re-read published manifest digest
conversionMetadata.conversionId: migration-conversion: plus lowercase SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON.stringify(["agent-mail/migration-conversion/v1",source_user_version,source_history_sha256,source_overlay_id,source_overlay_sha256,source_schema_sha256,target_registry_sha256,backup_id,backup_manifest_sha256,completed_at])
conversionMetadata.decoderAuthority: One strict decoder is shared by preflight, conversion, reopen, doctor, serialized-backup verification, empty restore, and full restore. It parses canonical JSON and rejects before trusting any stored component or record hash; re-encoding each parsed value must reproduce the exact stored JSON bytes.
conversionMetadata.historyDomain: source_history_json is an array of exact [safe positive integer version, nonempty string name, lowercase SHA-256 content hash] tuples, ordered contiguously from one. Every name/hash pair resolves to exactly one frozen semantic identity, identities are unique, the tuple sequence is one supported historical sequence, and source_user_version equals the final tuple version or zero only for the empty sequence.
conversionMetadata.schemaDomain: source_schema_json is an array of exact [type,name,tbl_name,sql] tuples where type is table, index, trigger, or view; name and tbl_name are nonempty strings; sql is a nonempty string; rows are strictly ordered by type,name,tbl_name,sql with no duplicate tuple or object identity. The complete tuple sequence must equal the in-memory sequence-derived base schema for decoded source_history_json before its digest is accepted.
conversionMetadata.overlayDomain: source_overlay_json is an exact seven-element v1 snapshot. The overlay id matches source_overlay_id; lease, progress, schema-object, source-row, and replacement-docsize tuple types and canonical order are exact; operation grammar and replacement derivation hold; the full expected FTS5 [type,name,tbl_name,sql] family, lease/progress/counter/source-row/indexed-row relations, recomputed source digests, and overlay classification all agree before its digest is accepted.
conversionMetadata.crossFieldRelations: The decoded history, source_user_version, schema, overlay id/snapshot, target registry, verified backup id/manifest digest/timestamp, conversion id, component digests, record encoding, and record digest must all identify one conversion. Recomputed hashes never excuse an invalid domain or cross-field relation.
forgedCases: self-consistent unknown or noncontiguous history with every dependent component, conversion, and record hash recomputed
self-consistent sequence-mismatched schema tuples with every dependent component, conversion, and record hash recomputed
self-consistent invalid overlay grammar or relation with every dependent component, conversion, and record hash recomputed
columns: conversion_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL
conversionMetadata.insertionGate: The exact persistent BEFORE INSERT trigger always aborts. Only inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE conversion transaction, after exact revalidation, verified-backup binding, and all semantic SQL checks, the converter verifies and drops that trigger, executes exactly one bound INSERT with changes=1, recreates and re-verifies the exact trigger, then commits. SQLite transactional DDL restores the closed trigger on rollback; every opener rejects a missing or altered gate.

conversionMetadata.immutability: Every opener and verifier compares the exact table, explicit unique index, and three trigger SQL bytes and hashes. It re-encodes every row, checks every component digest plus conversion_id and record_sha256, rejects duplicate source identities, and proves unauthorized INSERT plus all UPDATE and DELETE statements abort. Fresh databases contain the exact empty infrastructure.

preflightAuthority.sourceAccess: Never open the source database with SQLite before classification. lstat/open(O_RDONLY)/read only the canonical nonsymlink main database and existing -wal/-shm siblings; never create a missing path, chmod, lock, checkpoint, configure journaling, or touch a source sidecar.
preflightAuthority.sourceTreeSnapshotEncoding: UTF-8 JSON.stringify of recursively sorted [relative_path,type,dev,ino,mode,size,mtime_ns,ctime_ns,content_sha256_or_null] rows beneath privateRoot. content_sha256 is required for archive.sqlite, archive.sqlite-wal, archive.sqlite-shm, and every regular file in focused whole-tree fixtures; production may use null for unrelated large blob/journal/config files while retaining metadata.
preflightAuthority.scratchSnapshot: Copy the stable main database and optional WAL bytes into a newly created owner-only OS temporary directory outside privateRoot; do not copy SHM because it is a derived WAL index. Re-read source metadata and hashes after the copy and reject change. SQLite may create or modify sidecars only inside this unpublishable scratch directory, which is removed on every result.
classificationReads: SELECT version,name,content_hash FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version
SELECT exact conversion provenance columns FROM schema_migration_conversions ORDER BY conversion_id
preflightAuthority.sequenceSchemaDerivation: After strict history decoding, remap each recognized frozen semantic definition to the recorded contiguous position, execute that complete sequence in isolated in-memory SQLite, and derive the expected base-schema tuples. Compare exact tuples and their SHA-256 with the scratch database; no hand-authored object list participates.
preflightAuthority.baseSchemaTupleDomain: The projection contains every explicit table, index, trigger, and view tuple as [type,name,tbl_name,sql], strictly ordered by type,name,tbl_name,sql. Any arbitrary added object or any changed SQL/tbl_name/type/name is a mismatch even when all known objects remain present.
preflightAuthority.infrastructureExclusionGate: Before exclusion, schema_migrations must match the exact runner-derived DDL and decoded rows; conversion provenance must match all byte-frozen DDL and every row through the shared strict decoder; a reindex overlay must match one complete classified state and its full derived FTS5 tuples. Only those validated objects are removed from the base projection.
preflightAuthority.rejectionOrder: On the scratch connection, set only allowedPragmas, then reject corruption, newer version, missing/gapped/duplicate/unknown/mismatched history, placeholder, direct-SQL or schema fingerprint mismatch, invalid provenance, and invalid reindex overlay. Close and remove scratch before returning one stable error.
forbiddenBeforeSupportedClassification: opening the source database through SQLite
chmod, chown, rename, truncate, create, delete, lockfile, or sidecar creation
preflightAuthority.backupThenLock: For an exact supported legacy history, close/remove scratch, publish and independently verify the complete pre-conversion backup, acquire the exclusive application database-write admission barrier, and reject if any writer is active.
preflightAuthority.lockedRevalidation: While the exclusive barrier is held, take a second stable source snapshot and scratch classification. Require exact equality of user_version, history bytes/digest, base schema bytes/digest, overlay id/bytes/digest, provenance bytes/digest, and source database/WAL hashes with both the preflight decision and verified backup input. Any difference releases the barrier without opening the source read-write and restarts from preflight.
preflightAuthority.writeSequence: Only after locked revalidation may the opener enforce already-required owner-only permissions, open the source read-write without create, configure WAL and safe pragmas, verify the closed persistent conversion insert gate, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, revalidate the same logical fingerprint on that connection, convert, COMMIT, verify, and admit ordinary writers.
preflightAuthority.probeContract: For every reject class and success case, snapshot the whole focused private-root fixture and explicit main/WAL/SHM presence, bytes, mode, and link identity before/after. Rejection and preflight success leave them byte-for-byte identical; only scratch paths may appear and they are gone at return.

operationsAuthority.doctor: Doctor imports the canonical registry directly, uses the no-source-write preflight, and emits separate bounded evidence for invalid user_version, missing history, gap or duplicate, unknown name, checksum mismatch, noncanonical known history, conversion DDL/index/trigger or row/digest mismatch, unauthorized provenance shape, partial conversion, invalid reindex control DDL, invalid lease/progress/counter/replacement overlay, and newer schema. It never accepts caller-supplied migration definitions, touches source sidecars, or erases one finding behind another.
operationsAuthority.backup: The production backup service pauses all database writers, verifies exact canonical version 27, history, byte-exact conversion infrastructure and rows, and reindex overlay before serialization, then reopens the serialized snapshot and verifies the same bytes/digests. A valid active reindex overlay is resumable and may be backed up; a legacy, partial, corrupt, unknown, provenance-invalid, or newer database is not published as a new backup.
operationsAuthority.emptyRootRestore: Restore verifies manifest, artifact hashes, SQLite integrity, foreign keys, exact canonical version 27, exact canonical history, byte-exact conversion table/index/triggers and every row re-encoding/digest, and any active reindex overlay before the final rename. It never migrates or repairs a backup during restore.
operationsAuthority.fullRestore: Offline root replacement invokes the same registry verifier on the staged root before swap and again through repository verification after swap. Registry failure preserves the live root or rolls it back, with target, stage, and rollback disposition reported.
operationsAuthority.restoreAuthority: A historical backup must first be upgraded by the matching application version into a newly verified canonical backup. Restore does not infer or convert history.

requirements.text: Freeze every accepted semantic migration name, SQL checksum, execution mode, legacy declared version, and canonical slot.
Expose one contiguous canonical order from 1 through 27 and derive the next legal slot as 28.
Classify and convert every exact supported historical ledger without data loss or silent rewrite.
Route every writable production opener through the one registry and reject bypass.
Define fresh, create, upgrade, repeated-open, partial-failure, unknown, and newer-version behavior.
Reject unsafe histories from a disposable read-only preflight without opening or changing the source database, WAL, SHM, permissions, or private-root tree.
Freeze conversion provenance DDL, domains, encodings, insertion authority, immutability, and verification across every database operation.
Adopt the accepted unledgered reindex control schema and preserve every valid idle or resumable dynamic reindex state without treating arbitrary schema as canonical.
